target_customer: Leisure travelers and groups planning trips; paid Pro subscribers
problem: Travelers planned trips across docs, maps, email and spreadsheets. Wanderlog combines itinerary, map, reservations and collaboration in one app.
business_model: Freemium consumer subscription (annual Pro), with hotel booking links

founders.name: Harry Yu
founders.background_notes: Twin of Peter. YC lists the surname as Xu for Peter and Yu for Harry; TechCrunch and the company blog use Yu.

founders.name: Peter Xu
founders.background_notes: Earlier software engineer at Stripe per a profile.

competitors.name: Google Trips
competitors.what: Free Google trip organizer launched 2016 and shut down August 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Collaborative real-time editing, map routing, place data and email import are standard consumer app engineering with some hard parts for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Saved trips and collaboration give mild lock in, but travel planning features and place data are widely copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google discontinued Google Trips in August 2019, which opened a gap; Wanderlog's own posts position it as a replacement.

market_need_then: Group trip planning on scattered tools was common, and Google closing Trips in 2019 left a hole in free planners.

branding.domain_note: Uses wanderlog.com. Company was earlier called Travelchime and changed its name to Wanderlog.

identity.visual_style: Design led, with a map and itinerary view as core visual
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, practical: one app for all your travel planning needs.

rebrands.why: Not stated in sources found; date not found

branding.community_and_virality: Self reported 1M+ users, App of the Day on the App Store in November 2024, and press from NYT, WIRED and The Guardian listed on its homepage.

brand_strength.rationale: Good fit, easy name with strong app store ratings and press, but no evidence of a mascot, merch or community ritual.

outcome_analysis: Wanderlog launched in 2019 as Google Trips shut down, grew as a free app with an annual Pro tier, and raised only a 1.5M seed in 2021 from General Catalyst and Abstract. The company reports over a million users, and app analytics estimates vary widely. It looks capital efficient and still active, but revenue is not public and a later round was not found.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch and PhocusWire. Aggregators list a 150K pre-seed in March 2019 attributed to YC, unverified so not recorded as a round. Total funding estimates range from 1.5M to 2M. Competitor sources are 2024 and 2019 company blog posts, so dates are approximate. Usage and revenue figures come from the company homepage and app analytics estimates. TripIt (founded 2012 per Wanderlog blog) was a competitor but only a 2024 source was found, so it is left out of the dated list. Founder surname conflict: YC lists Peter Xu and Harry Yu; TechCrunch caption and company blog say Harry Yu; PhocusWire calls them brothers Peter and Harry Xu. Left as Harry Yu and Peter Xu (YC), disputed.
